provenance: English counterpart to the November 13 Japanese product overview, captured from the current web app in Storybook. The derivative question, answer, source and lesson are translated from content/answer.json and content/x-ad-en.json. Other UI data and learner identities are fixtures. No invitation was sent. Screens are still captures, with edited pacing and synthesized English narration.

scenes.title: Answers with a source you can revisit
scenes.summary: Read the answer. Rewatch the explanation.
sentences: An answer is more useful when you can check where it came from.
VideoQ can show the lecture video and time range behind an answer. Select the citation to jump to that explanation.
Read, rewatch, and listen again at your own pace. Some answers may not include citations.

scenes.title: Students ask in their own words
scenes.summary: Questions are answered from the videos in the course.
sentences: Invited students open the course with their own accounts.
They ask what they did not understand, in their own words.
The AI looks for relevant explanations across the course videos and answers from the lecture material. Answers use the course owner's allowance.

scenes.title: Start with a lecture video
scenes.summary: Upload a recording and choose its spoken language.
sentences: First, upload a lecture recording.
Choose the language spoken in the video. VideoQ transcribes the recording and prepares it for questions.
Once processing is complete, the video is ready to add to a course.

scenes.title: Bring related videos into one course
scenes.summary: Organize the material students will ask about.
sentences: Next, bring related videos together in a course.
Create a course for each teaching unit or training topic. Add videos from the library and arrange their order.
The course defines which learning materials students can ask about.

scenes.title: Invite the students who need access
scenes.summary: Sign in with the invited email, then accept the invitation.
sentences: Share a course with specific students by inviting their email addresses.
Students sign in with the verified email address that received the invitation, then accept it to join.
Members can watch and ask questions. They cannot edit the teaching materials. This screen is a demo; no invitation email was sent.

scenes.title: Keep your teaching material organized
scenes.summary: Find videos with tags. Review and edit transcripts.
sentences: Manage your recordings together in the video library. Use tags to organize them and find the videos you need.
Open a video's details to review its transcript.
You can also edit the subtitle text when a correction is needed.

scenes.title: Use student questions to improve your course
scenes.summary: Review saved answers and export the question history.
sentences: As the instructor, you can review saved questions and answers in the course history.
Questions from invited students include their username and email address. The student identity shown here is demo data.
Export the history as a CSV, or use the dashboard to review question trends and answer feedback.
Use what students find difficult to guide your next explanation or improve your course materials.

scenes.title: Connect the tools you already teach with
scenes.summary: YouTube imports, Moodle integration, and shared links.
sentences: VideoQ also supports importing videos from YouTube URLs and connecting with Moodle.
YouTube imports require your SearchAPI key. Moodle requires the dedicated plugin and connection settings.
For access without student registration, you can also choose a shared course link.

scenes.title: Let your lectures keep teaching
scenes.summary: Start with one video at videoq.jp/en
sentences: Upload, organize, share, answer, and reflect.
Turn your lecture videos into a learning partner.
Try VideoQ, starting with just one video.
